sessions.title: Professional Class
sessions.details: Our daily classes for professional-level dancers are led each week by a different artist from the international dance community. Each teacher brings their own style and technique to class, from their experience performing with world-leading dance companies and choreographers. With a strong focus on honing and maintaining technique, you’ll be challenged and inspired amongst peers. Professional class is ‘drop in’ and be booked by the day. You can still drop in and pay at Rambert, however as our spaces are strictly limited we recommend you book online before travelling to the building. Check out our line up for Autumn 2026 below: w/c 14th September – Sade Alleyne w/c 21st September – Benji Knapper w/c 28th September – Adel Balint w/c 5th October – Jack Anderson w/c 12th October – Phillip McDermott w/c 19th October – Jose Agudo w/c 26th October – Paxton Ricketts w/c 2nd November – Mickael Marso Riviere w/c 9th November – Charlotte Edmonds w/c 16th November – Thomas Page w/c 23rd November – Eileih Muir w/c 30th November – Georgia Tegou Terms and Conditions of Booking If you need to cancel your booking, you can do so up to 48 hours before a drop in for a full refund in class credits by logging into your Momence account. If you'd prefer a monetary refund, just email us to let us know.

sessions.title: Contemporary Beginners
sessions.details: In this contemporary class, you will be guided through the basics of contemporary technique while also exploring its Caribbean influences. Led by Rambert faculty member Paradigmz. He’s worked alongside choreographers across contemporary and classical African Peoples Dance, as well Jazz and Hip Hop and Modern Dance Forms and offers extensive experience. Artists and companies include Sakoba Dance Theatre, Jackie Guy, (Norman Rubber) Stephenson and many more. Suitable if: you’re 18+ and a beginner to contemporary dance, or maybe you’ve taken one or two classes before. This class features a live musician. Building Information Classes take place at Rambert, 99 Upper Ground SE1 9PP. We have a fully accessible building, including accessible toilets and showers. There is on-street parking for Blue Badge holders with step-free access to the building, and lifts to all levels. Changing facilities are available on the first floor. A water fountain is available on the second floor- please bring your own reuse-able bottle for this. You can wear whatever your are comfortable moving in, and you’re welcome to wear dance shoes if you have them (although no dark/black soles) or bare-feet. Please make sure you have removed jewellery before class, and long hair is tied back. Please note, as the studios are used by our professional dancers we ask that you refrain from using hair products and body lotions as these can make the floor slippery. Terms and Conditions of booking If you need to cancel your booking, you can do so up to 48 hours before a drop in and up to 48 hours before the first class of a term booking for a full refund in class credits by logging into your Momence account. If you'd prefer a monetary refund, just email us to let us know.

sessions.title: Pilates Open Level
sessions.details: This class covers most of the classical mat Pilates exercises but with a more contemporary approach and variations to train. Symeon’s teaching approach encourages you to learn how to make personal choices for your body and progress or regress according to your needs. Props are used to either challenge or simplify certain exercises. Suitable for: all if you are 18+, including complete beginners. Building Information Classes take place at Rambert, 99 Upper Ground SE1 9PP. We have a fully accessible building, including accessible toilets and showers. There is on-street parking for Blue Badge holders with step-free access to the building, and lifts to all levels. Changing facilities are available on the first floor. A water fountain is available on the second floor- please bring your own reuse-able bottle for this. You can wear whatever your are comfortable moving in, and you’re welcome to wear dance shoes if you have them (although no dark/black soles) or bare-feet. Please make sure you have removed jewellery before class, and long hair is tied back. Please note, as the studios are used by our professional dancers we ask that you refrain from using hair products and body lotions as these can make the floor slippery. Terms and Conditions of Booking If you need to cancel your booking, you can do so up to 48 hours before a drop in and up to 48 hours before the first class of a term booking for a full refund in class credits by logging into your Momence account. If you'd prefer a monetary refund, just email us to let us know.

sessions.title: Contemporary Intermediate
sessions.details: In this class, Belinda will guide you through a series of exercises which blend the use of torso, fall and recovery, spatial pathways, flow and momentum. Drawing from her training in Cunningham, Limon and Release techniques, class will start with short technical exercises that build into more complex travelling steps, dynamic swings and longer choreographic phrases. In this class a sense of community and shared experience is created, providing an environment where participants feel safe, challenge themselves and above all, have fun. Suitable if: you are 18+ and you’ve taken a few months of contemporary dance classes before, are comfortable with the basics, and would like to develop your technique and creativity. sessions.title: Ballet Beginners
sessions.details: In this Beginners class, Nandita will share the basics and foundations of Ballet technique with a healthy and holistic approach encouraging supportive alignment, functionality and efficiency, focus, balance, coordination and strength. sessions.title: YANG TO YIN
sessions.details: This class will flow through the energies of Yang into Yin. The first half will be focused on dynamic vinyasa-style asana to connect with and work the physical body through strong postures, an awareness of breath, a deep connection to sensation and body-mindfulness. The second half is designed to stimulate the parasympathetic nervous system with long floor-based postures, supported by meditation and mindfulness techniques to calm, ground and reset.

sessions.title: ProDance class with Maya Orchin
sessions.details: 'Alive Body' This high energy class is a mixture of structured improvisations and set choreography. We will be going in and out of the floor with full-bodied, athletic movement in a fast-paced environment. Bring a long sleeve shirt, trousers and knee pads if you have them. Come ready to move!

sessions.title: LATIN-FUSION DANCE
sessions.details: A joyful, high-energy class blending Latin dance styles with contemporary movement and expressive flow. In this 60-minute session, you’ll explore rhythm, musicality, and full-body movement through accessible choreography and playful combinations. Open to all levels, the class offers options and variations so you can move at your own pace—whether you’re new to dance or looking to deepen your groove. Expect a supportive atmosphere, a good sweat, and plenty of space to connect with the music, your body, and the joy of movement. No partner needed. Come as you are, leave energised and inspired.

sessions.title: FLOW & SOUND
sessions.details: A 60-minute practice combining mindful movement with the soothing vibrations of crystal singing bowls. The class begins with 45 minutes of Vinyasa Flow, linking breath and movement through a dynamic yet accessible sequence. Expect to build warmth, move with intention and create space in both body and mind. The final 15 minutes invite you to slow down and settle into deep relaxation, accompanied by the resonant tones and vibrations of crystal singing bowls. A chance to move, breathe and then simply be, leaving you feeling grounded, restored and refreshed. Suitable for all levels.

sessions.title: Flying Low
sessions.details: Developed by David Zambrano, Flying Low is a floorwork technique that teaches smooth transitions into and out of the floor using spirals, sliding, and fluid sequences. It builds the foundation for effortless connection between the body and its surroundings—integral to the art of Passing Through.

sessions.title: ProDance Class with Richard Chappell
sessions.details: Richard's class starts with mobilising, expanding and stretching the body through repetitive movement patterns and improvisational tasks, connecting to breath. After this, exercises are looped across the studio, connecting dancers to the ground and encouraging continuous passing of weight between the hands and feet. Spirals are used to build up momentum, coordination and precision and small phrases connect material together. The class concludes a full bodied and playful final phrase. Richard's class is designed to be energetic and challenging, whilst also being accessible and adaptable for different energy levels and needs.

Together, we will explore how to connect more deeply with ourselves, our bodies, and each other in a supportive and open environment. Through guided tasks and shared exploration, the class invites participants to discover joy in both dancing and witnessing others dance, while building a sense of community and connection. Rooted in playfulness and embodied practice, the sessions offer space to move freely, listen closely, and expand awareness through improvisation. Image by Yu-Ning Tan.

Through the gentle resonance of crystal singing bowls, immersive nature soundscapes and song, you’ll be invited to slow down, rest and reconnect. Held in a cosy, welcoming space, this is an opportunity to pause, let go of expectations and simply be. Come as you are, settle into the experience in your own way, and leave feeling grounded, restored and nourished.

Rather than training these qualities separately explore how to use them interchangeably, through motif development, grooves, floorwork, improvisation and choreography. How do these inform your character development, performance and choice of movement regardless of your style?

sessions.details: What if you could pursue your ambitions without constantly pushing yourself to the limit? A two-hour workshop for ambitious people who want to build meaningful careers and creative lives without success coming at the expense of their wellbeing. Together, we’ll explore Sustainable Ambition: a different way of thinking about achievement that makes space for ambition, creativity, rest and a deeper connection with ourselves. The workshop combines embodiment, Human Design and nervous system practices in a practical, reflective and conversation-based format. We’ll explore how we relate to pressure, productivity and achievement, and discover tools to help us work with ourselves rather than constantly pushing against ourselves. The first half of the workshop will focus on conversation, reflection and practical tools. In the second half, we’ll move into embodied movement practices, creating space to experience and integrate what we’ve explored. This workshop is particularly for creatives, freelancers and ambitious people navigating change, growth or demanding careers, and for anyone curious about finding a more sustainable way of working and living.

sessions.title: Countertechnique with Isabelle Nelson
sessions.details: The Countertechnique® class is a contemporary dance technique class. It stretches, coordinates and strengthens the body, making the dancer sweat, build stamina and really move. The class starts with a recurring set of exercises, allowing dancers to investigate the Countertechnique® principles in detail. The second half of the class consists of changing components, working towards luscious movement combinations and jumping at the end. By continuously and sequentially directing parts of the body away from each other in space, Countertechnique allows the moving dancer to work with an ever-changing dynamic balance. This dynamic balance reduces the pressure on the overall body structure and can be changed at any given moment.

sessions.title: YANG TO YIN
sessions.details: This class will flow through the energies of Yang into Yin. The first half will be focused on dynamic vinyasa-style asana to connect with and work the physical body through strong postures, an awareness of breath, a deep connection to sensation and body-mindfulness. The second half is designed to stimulate the parasympathetic nervous system with long floor-based postures, supported by meditation and mindfulness techniques to calm, ground and reset.

sessions.title: Moving Together: Improvisation, Connection & Expression
sessions.details: In this class, James guides participants through improvisation practices that encourage honesty, curiosity, and personal expression through movement. Together, we will explore how to connect more deeply with ourselves, our bodies, and each other in a supportive and open environment. Through guided tasks and shared exploration, the class invites participants to discover joy in both dancing and witnessing others dance, while building a sense of community and connection. Rooted in playfulness and embodied practice, the sessions offer space to move freely, listen closely, and expand awareness through improvisation. Image by Yu-Ning Tan.

sessions.title: FLOW & SOUND
sessions.details: A 60-minute practice combining mindful movement with the soothing vibrations of crystal singing bowls. The class begins with 45 minutes of Vinyasa Flow, linking breath and movement through a dynamic yet accessible sequence. Expect to build warmth, move with intention and create space in both body and mind. The final 15 minutes invite you to slow down and settle into deep relaxation, accompanied by the resonant tones and vibrations of crystal singing bowls. A chance to move, breathe and then simply be, leaving you feeling grounded, restored and refreshed. Suitable for all levels.

sessions.title: Gaga People
sessions.details: Gaga is the movement language developed by Ohad Naharin throughout many years, parallel to his work as a choreographer and artistic director (1990-2018) of Batsheva Dance Company. Gaga originated from Naharin’s need to communicate with his dancers and his curiosity in the ongoing research of movement. Gaga classes are predicated on a deep listening to the body and to physical sensations. The instructions are deployed to increase awareness of and further amplify sensation, and rather than turning from one prompt to another, information is layered, building into a multisensory, physically challenging experience. While many instructions are imbued with rich imagery, the research of Gaga is fundamentally physical, insisting on a specific process of embodiment. Inside this shared research, the improvisational nature of the exploration enables each participant’s deeply personal connection with Gaga. Throughout the class, participants are guided by a series of evocative instructions deployed to increase awareness of and further amplify sensation. Rather than turning from one prompt to another, information is layered, building into a multisensory, physically challenging experience. While many instructions are imbued with rich imagery, the research of Gaga is fundamentally physical, insisting on a specific process of embodiment. Inside this shared research, the improvisational nature of the exploration enables each participant’s deeply personal connection with Gaga. Participants should wear comfortable clothes and be prepared to dance barefoot or in socks. It is advisable to bring a bottle of water and a towel for use after class.

sessions.title: THE LYMPHATIC PRACTICE
sessions.details: Self-Lymphatic Drainage — Your Hands, Your Pace, Your Choice A guided introduction to self-lymphatic drainage and the foundational bodywork behind LYMPHLOVER. If you’ve joined one of Carli's. workshops before, this is an opportunity to return to the practice, deepen your understanding and explore the work further. If you’re new to lymphatic drainage, this is your starting point, offering clear, practical guidance on working with your own body through self-massage, palpation, skin movements and breathwork. We’ll explore the key areas that form the foundation of my practice, learning where to work, how to use your hands and why we follow a particular sequence. You’ll be guided through the practice, with time to explore, ask questions and notice what you feel. Come once to learn. Return to practise. Make the work your own. Your hands. Your pace. Your choice. How to Prepare: Wear something comfortable that allows you to move freely. Loose trousers, leggings or a crop top all work well. Avoid anything too tight. You can work over your clothing, underneath a loose T-shirt or directly on your skin with a little oil. It’s entirely up to you and what feels comfortable. If you’d like to use oil or cream, please bring a small amount from home. Something simple, such as rosehip or coconut oil, works well. This is a guided self-practice, so you’ll be using your own hands throughout the session. If you tend to feel cold, bring an extra layer or a pair of socks. The studios are generally warm, but your comfort matters. You’re also welcome to message us beforehand if there’s anything that would help you feel more at ease. About Carli: Carli is the founder of LYMPHLOVER and teaches self-lymphatic work through practical explanation, guided self-massage and breathwork. Her teaching brings together body awareness, practical physiology and perspectives from her Chinese medicine studies, helping people take an active role in caring for their own bodies.

sessions.title: Whirl and Climb - Dance-partnering  for children with a trusted person (1-3.5 years old)
sessions.details: Inspired by the instinctive movement, touch and curiosity that young children naturally express through play, this workshop invites parents and children to explore new ways of dancing, climbing, flying and moving together. Through playful improvisation and movement activities, we will develop a deeper awareness of our body language and explore different approaches to partnering, connection and physical communication. These practices will form the foundation for learning simple acrobatic tricks, integrated naturally into the flow of the class. Parents and children will also explore short partner choreographies, developing body awareness, coordination and movement memory along the way. For children, dancing with a trusted adult offers an empowering opportunity to express their creativity, discover new movement possibilities and connect with others. For parents, the workshop creates space to reconnect with their own bodies, share joyful movement experiences and learn, experiment and grow alongside their child. A playful, supportive space to connect, move and discover together!

Expect to build warmth, move with intention and create space in both body and mind. The final 15 minutes invite you to slow down and settle into deep relaxation, accompanied by the resonant tones and vibrations of crystal singing bowls. A chance to move, breathe and then simply be, leaving you feeling grounded, restored and refreshed. Suitable for all levels.

sessions.title: LATIN-FUSION DANCE
sessions.details: A joyful, high-energy class blending Latin dance styles with contemporary movement and expressive flow. In this 60-minute session, you’ll explore rhythm, musicality, and full-body movement through accessible choreography and playful combinations. Open to all levels, the class offers options and variations so you can move at your own pace—whether you’re new to dance or looking to deepen your groove. Expect a supportive atmosphere, a good sweat, and plenty of space to connect with the music, your body, and the joy of movement. No partner needed. Come as you are, leave energised and inspired.

sessions.title: Monday Beginners Level 1 (Course of 6 classes)
sessions.details: Acland Burghley School Sports Centre, Churchill Road, London, NW5 1AN • Mondays 07/09, 14/09, 21/09, 28/09, 05/10 and 12/10 from 6:30 to 8:30pm. Classes taught by Rick Nodine. The course is a carefully crafted syllabus that will support beginners in understanding the conceptual and physical world of Contact Improvisation (CI) so that they can trust their own opinions about what they want as they dive into the CI experience. Connecting with other people is at the core of this practice and you will learn how CI roots connection in the reality of touch and movement. Class 1) A talk about what CI is and what to expect from it, a lead somatic warm-up and a solo physical exploration about moving comfortably in close connection with the floor, exercises about communicating with a partner through touch and physical listening, discussion of consensual touch and freedom of choice in dancing, a space for questions and concerns to be expressed and addressed. Class 2) We will learn some simple patterns that open different body surfaces to meeting in contact. Exercises that clarify how to get in and out of dances will strengthen your agency in following your interests within a group. Class 3) Exercises about exchanging body weight with a partner will be the beginning of the thrill of taking risks, understanding that good communication leads to pleasure in weight exchange and a lack of communication leads to discomfort, feeling your strength and understanding your limits. Class 4) Exercises about how to fall safely, learning more CI vocabulary to expand possibilities in physical communication, building confidence in starting and ending dances. Class 5) Exercises about how to fall safely, learning more CI vocabulary to expand possibilities in physical communication, building confidence in starting and ending dances. Class 6) Understanding Jamming and how to decode its rules and etiquette, responses to specific questions and a discussion about transitioning to open classes and jams. Integrating previous learning into free dancing and connecting to fun and risk in movement. https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-svm23-20260907183000

sessions.title: Saturday CI Workshop: Parallel and Perpendicular
sessions.details: Acland Burghley School Sports Centre, Churchill Road, London, NW5 1AN • When we are standing our spine is perpendicular to the surface of the earth, when we lay down it is parallel to the floor but perpendicular to the force of gravity. This basic but essential awareness is key for the CI dancer. A somatic warmup exploring these themes in dance will get us started. We will build our technical exploration around two series of partnering exercises. One series is all about relations to a partner when your spines are parallel to each other. A second series will be about having a perpendicular relationship to your partner. Both groups of exercises will progress from safe, close to the floor material and develop into high flying aerial supports. Practicing at your own level will be encouraged and challenging yourself will be safely supported. The material is appropriate for most levels of experience but not for absolute beginners. The jam following the workshop will give you plenty of time to integrate the material or just have fun. https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-satal-20260912143000

sessions.title: Tuesday Intermediates Class & Jam (Course of 5 classes)
sessions.details: Acland Burghley School Sports Centre, Churchill Road, London, NW5 1AN • Tuesdays 15/09, 22/09, 29/09, 06/10 and 13/10 from 6:30 to 8:30pm. Classes taught by Rick Nodine. It is aimed at dancers willing to improve their embodied confidence, expand their technical CI skills and deepen their improvisational repertoire. It is designed to offer a platform for dancers who want to continue their CI journey beyond Beginners 1 and Beginners 2:Improvers and to Open Class dancers willing to learn the building blocks that I think are necessary for dancing the athletic side of CI. 3 sections: Floorwork, Partner Technique and Improvisation. Floorwork is solo training that involves agile and efficient pathways for moving from laying on the floor to standing and back again, forward and backward shoulder rolls, inversion and disorientation patterns and falling manoeuvres for safe landings at speed. These are the solo skills that make us brave and confident when we give our weight to a partner, fly through the air and organise our centre/pelvis to lift another dancer. In Partner technique, are reaping the benefits of repetition, working on classic CI patterns in iteration, so that we can unpack the hidden details that make them flow. In Improvisation practice I have been codifying common CI improvisational modes that we often use when we jam. By naming and practicing them we can improvise our dances with more awareness. https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-sf2rl-20260915183000

sessions.title: Bound & Unbound Weekend, Autumn Edition: Exploring the Edges of Contact Improvisation
sessions.details: Anatomie Studio, Arch 113 Unit 17 Station Passage, London, SE15 2JR • A three day intensive with Jamus Wood & Rick Nodine. Contact Improvisation, Shibari & BMC®. In this short Intensive we will take time to explore some of the territory at the edges of Contact Improvisation. Exploring aspects of the dance that often go unrecognised or don’t receive quality attention. Contact improvisation, led by Rick, will be at the heart of our practice and the ground of our shared language. We will spend the first part of our time together dropping into inner and outer awareness through Body Mind Centering® exercises and perspectives. The intention is to bring a felt sense of embodiment and a deep listening to our dance. Later we will draw inspiration from Shibari (Japanese Rope Play) with Jamus. Initially, we’ll focus on the sensations of our bodies in relation to one another, without ropes yet through physical limitations, exploring binding and unbinding, being held and being free. We will then introduce ropes, engaging in Ichinawa (one rope technique) to explore further the qualities of resistance and surrender, stillness and breath, gravity and flow. A key aspect of our workshop will be The Switch —a playful exploration of roles as we transition between being bound and binding with one’s body. We will slow down and zoom in, lingering in each role for some time. Also taking moments when neither of us are in a role. We will emphasise consent throughout our time together. Consent will be taught as a practice so that we can dance within our limits while finding and exploring our edges together. We’ll conclude each day with an exploratory jam, allowing space to integrate what we've explored and to express ourselves freely, weaving our individual journeys into a collective tapestry of creativity and joy. Join us in this supportive circle of explorers. Together, let’s celebrate the borders of Contact Improvisation with Shibari, deepening our connections through movement, trust and shared discovery. Limited tickets available https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-stf0y-20261016183000

A key aspect of our workshop will be The Switch —a playful exploration of roles as we transition between being bound and binding with one’s body. We will slow down and zoom in, lingering in each role for some time. Also taking moments when neither of us are in a role. We will emphasise consent throughout our time together. Consent will be taught as a practice so that we can dance within our limits while finding and exploring our edges together. We’ll conclude each day with an exploratory jam, allowing space to integrate what we've explored and to express ourselves freely, weaving our individual journeys into a collective tapestry of creativity and joy. Join us in this supportive circle of explorers. Together, let’s celebrate the borders of Contact Improvisation with Shibari, deepening our connections through movement, trust and shared discovery. sessions.title: Monday Beginners Level 1+2 (Course of 12 classes)
sessions.details: Acland Burghley School Sports Centre, Churchill Road, London, NW5 1AN • Mondays 07/09, 14/09, 21/09, 28/09, 05/10 and 12/10 (Beginners 1) And Mondays 02/11, 09/11, 16/11, 23/11, 30/11 and 07/12 (Beginners 2) from 6:30 to 8:30pm. Classes taught by Rick Nodine. Beginners 1: The course is a carefully crafted syllabus that will support beginners in understanding the conceptual and physical world of Contact Improvisation (CI) so that they can trust their own opinions about what they want as they dive into the CI experience. Connecting with other people is at the core of this practice and you will learn how CI roots connection in the reality of touch and movement. Class 1) A talk about what CI is and what to expect from it, a lead somatic warm-up and a solo physical exploration about moving comfortably in close connection with the floor, exercises about communicating with a partner through touch and physical listening, discussion of consensual touch and freedom of choice in dancing, a space for questions and concerns to be expressed and addressed. Class 2) We will learn some simple patterns that open different body surfaces to meeting in contact. Exercises that clarify how to get in and out of dances will strengthen your agency in following your interests within a group. Class 3) Exercises about exchanging body weight with a partner will be the beginning of the thrill of taking risks, understanding that good communication leads to pleasure in weight exchange and a lack of communication leads to discomfort, feeling your strength and understanding your limits. Class 4) Exercises about how to fall safely, learning more CI vocabulary to expand possibilities in physical communication, building confidence in starting and ending dances. Class 5) Exercises about how to fall safely, learning more CI vocabulary to expand possibilities in physical communication, building confidence in starting and ending dances. Class 6) Understanding Jamming and how to decode its rules and etiquette, responses to specific questions and a discussion about transitioning to open classes and jams. Integrating previous learning into free dancing and connecting to fun and risk in movement. Beginners 2: This course will build on what we started in Beginners 1, deepening your understanding of the basics and developing more vocabulary for giving and receiving weight, moving in close connection with the floor, rolling and falling. We will work on expanding confidence in: Expressing what you want and do not want in your partner dances Creativity and playfulness Starting and finishing dances Deep physical listening Dancing in trios Lifting and being lifted Jamming skills I will be working with new material, so it will be a way of revisiting the fundamentals while learning new pathways. https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-sc3xz-20261102183000

sessions.title: Tuesday Intermediates Class & Jam (Course of 5 classes)
sessions.details: Acland Burghley School Sports Centre, Churchill Road, London, NW5 1AN • Tuesdays 10/11, 17/11, 24/11, 01/12 and 08/12 from 6:30 to 8:30pm. Classes taught by Rick Nodine. This course is aimed at dancers willing to improve their embodied confidence, expand their technical CI skills and deepen their improvisational repertoire. It is designed to offer a platform for dancers who want to continue their CI journey beyond Beginners 1 and Beginners 2:Improvers and to Open Class dancers willing to learn the building blocks that I think are necessary for dancing the athletic side of CI. 3 sections: Floorwork, Partner Technique and Improvisation. Floorwork is solo training that involves agile and efficient pathways for moving from laying on the floor to standing and back again, forward and backward shoulder rolls, inversion and disorientation patterns and falling manoeuvres for safe landings at speed. These are the solo skills that make us brave and confident when we give our weight to a partner, fly through the air and organise our centre/pelvis to lift another dancer. In Partner technique, are reaping the benefits of repetition, working on classic CI patterns in iteration, so that we can unpack the hidden details that make them flow. In Improvisation practice I have been codifying common CI improvisational modes that we often use when we jam. By naming and practicing them we can improvise our dances with more awareness. https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-s7ulz-20261110183000

sessions.details: Acland Burghley School Sports Centre, Churchill Road, London, NW5 1AN • Workshop taught by Guest Teacher Lalitaraja, dancer, CI teacher and meditation teacher. Minding the gap… [ ] What’s the point of meditation for CI dancers? One answer might be to train ourselves to recognise the gaps in our attention, where we lose the dance and forget to listen. One of the goals of meditation is to come into direct relationship with our lived experience. Short meditative exercises exploring relaxed awareness, clear knowing and engaging the heart mixed in with plenty of dancing. [ ] In her Underscore Nancy Stark Smith identified a gap as a “temporary absence of reference”. This course is aimed at dancers willing to improve their embodied confidence, expand their technical CI skills and deepen their improvisational repertoire. It is designed to offer a platform for dancers who want to continue their CI journey beyond Beginners 1 and Beginners 2:Improvers and to Open Class dancers willing to learn the building blocks that I think are necessary for dancing the athletic side of CI. 3 sections: Floorwork, Partner Technique and Improvisation. Floorwork is solo training that involves agile and efficient pathways for moving from laying on the floor to standing and back again, forward and backward shoulder rolls, inversion and disorientation patterns and falling manoeuvres for safe landings at speed. These are the solo skills that make us brave and confident when we give our weight to a partner, fly through the air and organise our centre/pelvis to lift another dancer. In Partner technique, are reaping the benefits of repetition, working on classic CI patterns in iteration, so that we can unpack the hidden details that make them flow. In Improvisation practice I have been codifying common CI improvisational modes that we often use when we jam. By naming and practicing them we can improvise our dances with more awareness. https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-s7ulz-20261124183000

sessions.title: Monday Beginners Level 1+2 (Course of 12 classes)
sessions.details: Acland Burghley School Sports Centre, Churchill Road, London, NW5 1AN • Mondays 07/09, 14/09, 21/09, 28/09, 05/10 and 12/10 (Beginners 1) And Mondays 02/11, 09/11, 16/11, 23/11, 30/11 and 07/12 (Beginners 2) from 6:30 to 8:30pm. Classes taught by Rick Nodine. Beginners 1: The course is a carefully crafted syllabus that will support beginners in understanding the conceptual and physical world of Contact Improvisation (CI) so that they can trust their own opinions about what they want as they dive into the CI experience. Connecting with other people is at the core of this practice and you will learn how CI roots connection in the reality of touch and movement. Class 1) A talk about what CI is and what to expect from it, a lead somatic warm-up and a solo physical exploration about moving comfortably in close connection with the floor, exercises about communicating with a partner through touch and physical listening, discussion of consensual touch and freedom of choice in dancing, a space for questions and concerns to be expressed and addressed. Class 2) We will learn some simple patterns that open different body surfaces to meeting in contact. Exercises that clarify how to get in and out of dances will strengthen your agency in following your interests within a group. Class 3) Exercises about exchanging body weight with a partner will be the beginning of the thrill of taking risks, understanding that good communication leads to pleasure in weight exchange and a lack of communication leads to discomfort, feeling your strength and understanding your limits. Class 4) Exercises about how to fall safely, learning more CI vocabulary to expand possibilities in physical communication, building confidence in starting and ending dances. Class 5) Exercises about how to fall safely, learning more CI vocabulary to expand possibilities in physical communication, building confidence in starting and ending dances. Class 6) Understanding Jamming and how to decode its rules and etiquette, responses to specific questions and a discussion about transitioning to open classes and jams. Integrating previous learning into free dancing and connecting to fun and risk in movement. Beginners 2: This course will build on what we started in Beginners 1, deepening your understanding of the basics and developing more vocabulary for giving and receiving weight, moving in close connection with the floor, rolling and falling. We will work on expanding confidence in: Expressing what you want and do not want in your partner dances Creativity and playfulness Starting and finishing dances Deep physical listening Dancing in trios Lifting and being lifted Jamming skills I will be working with new material, so it will be a way of revisiting the fundamentals while learning new pathways. https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-sc3xz-20261130183000

sessions.title: Contact Improvisation WORKSHOP w/ Ezra LeBank "Cloud Tectonics"
sessions.details: Laban Building - Car Park Studio, Creekside, London, SE8 3DZ • Cloud Tectonics: Training for Contact Improvisation & Contemporary Partnering “Is it possible for us to fly and fall without noticing much? Can the drift inherent in momentum compel us toward intuitive pathways above and along each other? We will begin with Dirt Work, physical training to expand, integrate, and ready our bodies in conversation with gravity and the earth. This prepares us for flight and dynamic capacity we explore in Cloud Tectonics, training that reframes our experiences of lift, loft, and drift. Detailed and buoyant exercises guide us toward a dancing experience full of abundant and radically free choice-making in vertical and spherical space for both ourselves and those we dance with. We imagine a dance we co-create amidst simultaneous independence and communion in flight. Ezra LeBank is a Professor of Movement and Chair of the Department of Theatre Arts at California State University Long Beach. Meditation, Aikido, and acrobatics work their way into his curiosity of CI. His approach is inspired by many wonderful teachers including Nancy Stark Smith, Ray Chung, Mike Vargas, Nita Little, and Steve Paxton. He has been invited as a teacher at International Contact Festival Freiburg, West Coast Contact Improv Jam, Seattle Festival for Dance Improvisation, Poland Contact Festival, Oberlin CI@50, and many more. Through his research company Bad Goat Dance, he studies Dirt Work & Cloud Tectonics as methods of bringing ourselves closer to the earth and to each other. www.badgoatdance.com https://bookwhen.com/cigoldsmiths/e/ev-sim4j-20261018110000

sessions.title: Monday Contact Improv: Class + Jam
sessions.details: Rose Lipman Building, 43 De Beauvoir Road, London, N1 5SQ • Doors open at 6.20pm Please note they won't be an intro circle anymore. First timers can arrive a bit earlier for any questions and info around consent or about the jam. I also advise newcomers to familiarise themselves with the guidelines. This week we have a class taught by Marie, an experienced CI practitioner (22 years), professional dancer and choreographer. Theme and Content The theme of the class will be posted closer to the time in the CI Monday Jam WhatsApp group. You can join in following this link: https://chat.whatsapp.com/Iivbz8LzDvK5lGkiitQgcH (please note I will ask you a few question about yourself before I allow you into the chat, when you join please introduce yourself so we know who's in the chat) These Contact Improvisation classes give participants tools to be in touch and communicate through touch, and feel more confident joining a jam. There are open levels and benefit beginners, improvers and experienced practitioners. There is a mix of somatic guided exploration to be embodied, usually in solo, some mindful and focused explorations with one or several partners, and some more technical tools or short patterns. This will be followed by a 45min-1h jam Jam The emphasis of the jam is to explore movement while being in physical contact with other movers. Participants are encouraged to experience it as an embodied research and a practice where everyone can bring their own research, interest and physicality into the space. Jamming is the best way to try out, take risks, learn from each other, observe, connect, be surprised, practice setting boundaries, dance and play with people we may not know or expect to dance with. Participants are asked to take responsibility for themselves. Levels and abilities: The space welcomes professional dancers, amateurs, seasoned contact improvisers and beginners, people from all backgrounds and abilities. It requires every participants to take responsibility for their own bodies, so if you need extra support or a carer or someone to look after you then you can bring them for free. Note for beginners: the jam is not guided. The facilitator is there to hold the space but doesn't guide the jam. What is Contact Improvisation (CI)? Contact Improvisation is movement research that explores the physical principles of touch, momentum, and shared weight in relation to gravity. It involves a constant dialogue between two or more movers who respond to each other’s movements in real time, often maintaining physical contact but also playing with proximity and space. This practice emphasises spontaneity, trust, and mutual awareness, allowing dancers to create unique movement for each encounter. sessions.title: Contact Improvisation - Beginner's course (+strengthen CI skills)
sessions.details: Rose Lipman Building, 43 De Beauvoir Road, London, N1 • Dates: Sept 24th to November 19th This course is for anyone curious about Contact Improvisation. It is open to both beginner dancers and those who have a bit more experience and want to revisit the fundamentals and strengthen their CI skills. Over 8 weeks you will learn to share weight and communicate through dance with the group or in partners. By the end of the course you should have the tools to join a Contact Improvisation jam and move confidently with other dancers. Each week, we will co-create a playful and safe space for experimentation and exploration. Every class will start with games and tasks to awaken our awareness of inner and outer space. Followed by integrating basic skills of Contact Improvisation in a simple and guided way. Practicing falling, rolling, floating, lifting and supporting, using gravity to move effortlessly. We will approach other themes such as touch and no touch, following and leading, support, structures and lifts (low table and high table), centre and extremities, shared weight and shared balance, upside down, head to tail connection, dynamics, and momentum. Please wear comfortable clothes. NB: the class on November 19th will take place at Chisenhale Dance Space 7-9pm (no wheelchair access) There is no class on October 29th If you have any financial difficulties please get in touch with me directly mariechabert@orange.fr https://bookwhen.com/mariechabert/e/ev-su748-20260924183000

sessions.title: SOFT WORLDS - Movement, Poetry and Collective Imagination
sessions.details: Chisenhale Dance Space, 64-84 Chisenhale Road, London, E3 5QZ • SOFT WORLDS Movement, Poetry and Collective Imagination A pillow can be a place to rest, a partner to move with, a creature or a landscape. What sensations, images and stories might it invite? Join dance artist Marie Chabert and artist-anthropologist Rich Thornton for a three-hour research workshop exploring pillows, movement and words. Building on our research at Rambert Playground last September, we’ll explore the materiality and imagery of these familiar objects through movement, touch and play. Discovering how their weight, softness and shape can offer ways to move and interact with one another. Along the way, we’ll experiment with words and poetry, discovering how they might emerge from, accompany or change our dances. An invitation to follow our curiosity and see what we imagine together. Please note unfortunately there's no wheelchair access to the building. If you have any access needs you can communicate with us prior to the event. Bios Rich Thornton Rich Thornton is an artist anthropologist and theatre director who uses traditional and multimodal ethnographic methods to explore subjectivity, ethics, theatre and education. As a social anthropologist, his work involves a critical inquiry into how people navigate their cultural, political and emotional worlds, with a particular interest in how individuals make sense of who they are in the world. For Rich, theatre is a way of being. Alongside writing, producing and performing theatre as part of his autoethnographic inquiry, he explores how the principles of participatory theatre can be used within anthropology. He also facilitates workshops using theatre tools and games to connect theories, emotions and empirical data through body-focused storytelling. www.richthornton.com Marie Chabert Marie Chabert is a performer, choreographer, Contact Improviser and teacher whose work is rooted in collaboration and multidisciplinary practice. Her artistic research explores the relational dynamics of touch, space, bodies, gravity and liveness through somatic and experiential approaches. She brings text into dialogue with movement, creating interactive and site-specific performances that explore audience co-creation and make the space between performer and viewer tangible and malleable. Her choreographic work has been presented internationally, including at Tanzfabrik Berlin, Art Omi in NY, The Place, Open Art Freiburg, Biennale de la Danse Off Lyon, Rimbun Dahan in Malaysia, Toplocentrala in Bulgaria, and Centro Nacional de la Danza in Mexico. As a performer, she has worked with artists and companies including Fin Walker, Kate Flatt, Freddie Opoku-Addaie, Retina Dance Company, Katie Green, Jean Abreu, Vera Tussing and Lionel Hoche, and has performed at the Royal Ballet and Opera. Marie curates the Monday Contact Improvisation Jam and Women’s Touch. She is also co-founder of The Godet, a collective with Thomas Broda and Danny Kearns creating work at the intersection of dance, live music and physical theatre. She holds a BA in Contemporary Dance from London Contemporary Dance School and an MA in Creative Practice from Trinity Laban and Independent Dance. She is a recipient of the Gill Clarke Bursary and a Leverhulme scholarship. mariechabert.com https://bookwhen.com/mariechabert/e/ev-sl3n2-20261108130000

It requires every participants to take responsibility for their own bodies, so if you need extra support or a carer or someone to look after you then you can bring them for free. Note for beginners: the jam is not guided. The facilitator is there to hold the space but doesn't guide the jam. What is Contact Improvisation (CI)? Contact Improvisation is movement research that explores the physical principles of touch, momentum, and shared weight in relation to gravity. It involves a constant dialogue between two or more movers who respond to each other’s movements in real time, often maintaining physical contact but also playing with proximity and space. This practice emphasises spontaneity, trust, and mutual awareness, allowing dancers to create unique movement for each encounter. sessions.title: **Women’s Touch : Skin stories with Vanio Papadelli**
sessions.details: Siobhan Davies Studios, 85 Saint George's Road, London, SE1 6ER • Embodiment - Community - Develop self-enquiry and agency- Be in touch - Share reflection + Experiences + Food What stories do our bodies carry? How do we move and encounter one another through our skinscape? In this edition of Women’s Touch, Marie Chabert and Vanio Papadelli invite you to explore the body as a living landscape carrying sensations, memories, traces, restrictions and possibilities. First we'll explore various ways of touching and responding to touch, tuning to our sensing and listening body. We will then co-create a temporary archive of body stories, tracing, writing and responding through touch, mapping sensations, witnessing dances and allowing words and sounds to emerge. What is Women's Touch? Women’s touch is an event curated by Marie Chabert, that offers a space for those who identify as women and non-binary to explore movement practices that are mainly based on touch (Contact Improvisation, somatic practices, improvisation) in a safe environment. It aims to empower women to claim their space and redefine it within a framework that challenges prevailing patriarchal norms. It offers both a place to embody and share our experiences verbally. The intention is to foster a supportive environment, where women and non-binary participants feel safe to take risks, be vulnerable, and share their humanity, free from the pressure of dominant dynamics. Cultivating such spaces requires trust, shared language, and mutual care. It allows us not just to survive, but to thrive in connection. About Vanio Papadelli I am an interdisciplinary performance artist and educator based in London. I teach across HE Performing Arts Institutions (mainly Rose Bruford College and Trinity Laban Conservatoire of Music and Dance) and as a freelancer. With movement and the senses at the core of my practice, I interact with other media including text, video, everyday objects and natural materials to create intimate, multi-layered, poetic and surreal environments as spaces of connection, reminiscence and change. My artistic practice explores raw and tender territories of vulnerability, memory, care and candidness in human relationships imbued in more-than-human worlds. I have dealt especially with mother-daughter relationships, female friendships, experiences of giving birth and mothering. My work is based in collaborative and interdisciplinary processes and has travelled in Greece, UK, Italy, Poland, Germany, Egypt and Lebanon. https://vaniopapadelli.com/ Who is this for? Those who identify as women and non-binary interested in bringing more awareness to physical interactions in dancing and in Contact Improvisation It welcomes all levels and can be applied to other practices than Contact Improvisation. In the past people were able to apply it to dance therapy, theatre, psychology... This lab is open level. No prior experience of Contact Improv is required If you have financial difficulties and want to take part, please get in touch. photo by Sol Ji Park https://bookwhen.com/mariechabert/e/ev-s61bh-20261122110000

sessions.title: Moving Encounters - An experiential workshop exploring embodied relational awareness for therapists and practitioners
sessions.details: Centre 151, 151 Whiston Road, London, E2 8GU • A one-day experiential workshop for therapists and practitioners - exploring how body, attention, and relation shape the way we work. This is a guided and contained space for working with attention, sensation, movement, and relation as they arise in real time. The emphasis is on direct experience rather than interpretation, performance, or technique. The day is structured, but not prescriptive, allowing space for both individual exploration and relational processes with others. The atmosphere of the day - The workshop provides a structured experiential setting for exploring how awareness is organised in the body and in relation. At times the work will be internally focused and quiet. At other times it will involve movement in relation to others, with clear frameworks supporting consent, choice, and pacing throughout. Throughout the day, the intention is to stay close to what is actually happening in experience, moment by moment. Approaches informing the work - This workshop draws on principles from: Body-Mind CenteringⓇ — somatic and developmental awareness of the body Authentic Movement — witnessed movement and reflective awareness Contact Improvisation — weight, responsiveness, and relational movement These are not taught as techniques, but used as reference points within structured experiential inquiry. What will be explored - Across the day, the work will include: attention to sensation, impulse, and movement how awareness shifts between self and other relational contact and distance witnessing and being witnessed patterns of responsiveness in interaction how experience registers in the body Participation is always invitational, and there is space to observe or pause at any time. Who this is for - Participants often find that working in this way opens new dimensions of attunement and presence that directly enrich their clinical or facilitation work. The workshop is open to therapists, counsellors, psychotherapists, and practitioners working in relational or embodied contexts. It is designed for those interested in exploring embodied awareness as part of their reflective practice, particularly those curious about how bodily experience shapes presence, attention, and relational responsiveness. No previous movement or dance experience is required. What this is not - This is not: a dance or performance workshop a training in any therapeutic modality a group therapy or personal process group a space for psychological interpretation or treatment It is an experiential workshop for embodied inquiry and relational exploration. Reflection and integration -There will be structured opportunities to reflect verbally on experience during the day. Reflection is offered as a way of noticing and articulating experience, rather than interpreting or analysing it. Participants are encouraged to consider how the work may relate to their own professional practice. Access Needs -the venue is on a ground floor with accessible toilets. If you have specific access needs please don't hesitate to get in touch. About the facilitator - This workshop is facilitated by Mark Rietema, a UKCP-registered Psychotherapist, and Somatic Movement Therapist (BMCA) with a background spanning clinical practice, somatic education, and movement facilitation. Alongside a clinical practice that has included extensive work within NHS mental health services, Mark teaches and facilitates in a range of professional and academic contexts, including Embody-Move UK, Institut Prozessarbeit Deutschland, and King's College London, where he contributed to research on arts and wellbeing in higher education. He teaches Body-Mind Centering within official BMCⓇ trainings in the UK, Spain, and Italy. Mark also teaches Contact Improvisation nationally and internationally, and is part of the organising team of the London Contact Festival and CI@Goldsmiths. This direct grounding in CI practice informs the relational and movement dimensions of the workshop. A background in community arts (MA, Goldsmiths) and experience facilitating internationally - including in the USA, Palestine, and Germany - continues to shape an approach that is both rigorous and attentive to the lived complexity of group work. His training in Process Work (Mindell) informs the way the group field and emerging process are held throughout the day. Mark will be supported throughout the day by Sole de la Hoz, a Contact Improvisation teacher and trainee psychotherapist in Process Oriented Psychology, with a professional background in dance. sessions.title: Weaving Spatial Support into the Body, Laura Doehler
sessions.details: Rockingham Community Centre, Falmouth Rd, London SE1 6PD, UK • In this workshop we will explore how our weight always is supported by default and acts as support simply through being in space and sensing our own physical space. We strip back expectations around support to uncover how a changing physical landscape of body and space create a container that at times carries us through space and at other times means we become a carrier or both. Our intention is to challenge our ideas around support so we won't get locked into carrying or loading and acquire greater skills in falling through letting go and expansion. We will probe spatial anchoring by tapping into the expansive qualities that space offers, find lightness and the ability to redirect oneself. These processes shall support a greater freedom in our dancing inside and outside the studio as we reckon with our ideas and expectations around support.

A CI jam to bring everyone together: London's CI teachers, organisers and you, the wider community for a time out to dance, lab and connect.


26th: Saturday 16:00 - 22:00

27th: Sunday 11:00-17:00


Our teaching and organising community is the foundation of London's CI community.
We want to celebrate being here together and meet you as a community, not just as individual practitioners.

Join us for one or two days of dancing, where you can fully let go—fall, fly, and be caught by the fabric of long-term, lush CI practices that our community holds. Experience CI as life integration where body meets mind and generates a collective field of care, curiosity and spirit.

We enter with as little agenda as possible, honouring the present moment that improvisation and jamming invite. Each day will be centred around spacious jams in the large Walworth Hall. Adjacent areas—the kitchen, living room, chill-out space and courtyard—give us room to chat, eat, rest, dream, and flow.

As our dancing and teaching community grows in size, practices, wisdom, and challenges, this event offers us a chance to jam our way into sensing who we are now and how we step into the future together.

Before and during the event, you are invited to share any questions you have about CI—technical, visionary, reflective, or concerning needs or serious concerns. We will dedicate 1.5 hours each day for teachers to explore these questions in small, spontaneous labs that you’re welcome to join on the spot.

And that’s really all there is to it!

This event is for people who consider CI an ongoing practice and who want to connect with the wider community through shared research and continuous exploration.

Please bring your own food. A microwave, cups, tea, and basic kitchen essentials are available to support your day.

sessions.title: "SENSATIONAL MOVES": 9 -12 April . 4 DAY INTENSIVE Feldenkrais, Movement Exploration & CI with Simonetta Alessandri & Thomas Kampe
sessions.details: Room 154, Richard Hoggart Building, Goldsmiths, Lewisham Way, London, SE14 6NW • 9 -12 April 4 day Intensive exploring somatic dance practice, Feldenkrais Method and Contact Improvisation. In this four-day workshop, we combine somatic movement principles of the Feldenkrais Method® with dance exploration & Contact Improvisation practice. In the morning sessions we will be using ‘Awareness Through Movement’® lessons and touch-based explorations. We will focus on solo explorations and will connect with our core and imagination, deepening our felt sense of gravity and grounding. Through Dance Improvisational practice we will develop our observation skills and individual creative agency to integrate our embodied discoveries, fostering creative risk-taking and playfulness. In the afternoon sessions we will expand these explorations into the practice of Contact Improvisation to enhance our ability to interact and communicate expressively and playfully with ease and clarity. Drawing on our felt sense and somatic attunement through touch and gravity, we will revisit and refine Contact Improvisation skills and creative vocabularies, such as weight exchange, balance, support and lifts with a partner and in small ensemble situations. Each day we will take time to discuss or write reflectively about our personal and somatic discoveries. The Feldenkrais Method®, developed by Dr. Moshe Feldenkrais (1904-1984) is a gentle, embodied process focused on self-discovery, embodied thinking, creative wellbeing, and functional improvement. It invites participants to slow down, listen to internal sensations, and create new neural pathways that support creative choice making in action. This workshop is open to anyone interested in deepening their dance or movement practice. Thomas and Simonetta have been teaching Feldenkrais-informed dance classes around the globe for over 20 years and are world-leading researchers and artists in the field. Dr.Thomas Kampe (PhD) (he/him) has worked as a performer, artist, researcher and somatic educator across the globe for 40 years and was ‘Professor of Somatic Performance and Education’ at Bath Spa University (UK) between 2012 and 2022. Thomas initially trained in visual art and dance and is a teacher of the Feldenkrais Method ® which forms a rich foundation for his teaching, arts practice and research. He is interested in critical somatic arts legacies and his writings and performance works have been published internationally. He was editor of the Feldenkrais Research Journal Vol. 6 ‘Practices of Freedom: The Feldenkrais Method & Creativity’ in 2019, and recently co-edited JDSP Vol. 13.1 & 2 (2022): ‘Embodying Eco-Consciousness: Somatics, Aesthetic Practice and Social Action’. Simonetta Alessandri is an Italian dance artist & somatic educator based in London. She applies the Feldenkrais Method in dance & movement training and in performance making. She teaches at Trinity Laban, Goldsmiths University and London Contemporary Dance School. Her work is informed by more than 30 years of dancing, teaching and choreographing. Her choreography has been for dance companies, student pieces, large scale opera, improvised performance, site specific and movement direction for theatre. She was one of the few dance practitioners in Italy who began working with CI in the 90’s. She has been a guest teacher in Germany, Colombia, UK, Norway, Israel, France, Switzerland, Italy, Poland, Spain and Taiwan. She obtained the Post Graduate Diploma at London Contemporary Dance School; she is a qualified teacher of the Feldenkrais Method and she holds the Teacher Certificate of the Royal Academy of Dance. She is a founder member of CI@Goldsmiths London. https://bookwhen.com/cigoldsmiths/e/ev-swh5j-20260409100000

sessions.title: London CI Weekender - 2-days of Contact Improvisation, Exploring the concepts of 'reaching and meeting' and 'elements of the jam' w/ Josh Jones and Lily Antonia
sessions.details:
Willesden, London, UK •

London CI Weekender
A 2-day Contact Improvisation Workshop

https://dandelion.events/e/londonciweekender

Whats on offer :

A weekend of movement, exploration, co-collaboration and connection. Diving into the fundamentals & philosophy of Contact Improvisation. The London CI weekender offers space and guidance to engage with the practice, tune into the body & develop the skills that serve us both in the dance and in daily life. Bringing shared inquiry to the foreground to drop deeper through the layers of what is possible through CI.

Each day has a distinct focus, and participants are welcome to attend either day or the full weekend.

Come deepen your connection to the ground, space, and others while gaining tools for (contact) improvisation, jamming, and attuned awareness through the joy of movement.

Saturday: Reaching & Meeting

How can we meet the earth, meet ourselves and meet another?

How is it to be met?

Investigating and understanding mutual meeting as a core part of the dance.

Reaching as a tool to transform into oscillating expansive movers. To expand awareness and expand the ability of the body. Coming away from collapse and into lightness. Effortlessly working with gravity and momentum.

The day will include technical insights and the approach is practice as research. Allowing ourselves to be informed by the dance - discover how to move functionally and fluidly, open to all that's available in the present. Through solo, partner & group exercises we’ll explore reaching and meeting as a shared point of attention.

This day offers a grounding in presence, deep listening, and mutual direction.

Sunday: Elements of the Jam


On Sunday, we move into the world of the jam. We’ll explore how to enter and exit dances, navigate shared space, and respond to each unfolding moment. Through structured improvisation scores and instant compositions, we’ll build tools for the jam, develop adaptability, and co-create through group improvisation.

A container for emergence and spontaneity.

Meet your facilitators

Lily Antonia (She/Her)

Dance & Movement Artist | Facilitator

Lily is a contemporary dance artist, specialising in contact improvisation. She has been performing, teaching and choreographing internationally since graduating from Trinity Laban Conservatoire of Music and Dance. Working with companies Wired Aerial Theatre, Mad Dogs Dance Theatre, and Company Chameleon. Lily is co-director of contemporary dance and live art company UMAMI-i!-MOVEMENT and co-founder of Contact Improv MCR.

Her approach to CI blends playful exploration with technical clarity. Inviting curiosity, challenging potential and nurturing individual creativity - Lily invites dancers to bring an aliveness to the present. Creating spaces where dancers can listen, trust, and move with intention and spontaneity.

“To cultivate a state of being - in readiness without anticipation... we open ourselves to

all possibilities"

Joshua Jarvis Jones (He/They)

Dancer | Facilitator | Choreographer

Josh is a contemporary dancer and facilitator whose practice is rooted in emotional exploration and embodied connection. Following a time of personal loss, he found dance—especially contact improvisation—as a vital tool for healing, grounding, and rediscovering relationships with self and others.

Trained at the Northern School of Contemporary Dance, Josh has performed internationally with artists like Ricardo Buscarini and Madeline Shan, exploring themes of intimacy and identity. His deep engagement with contact improvisation bridges technique and relational psychology, and he shares this through workshops, labs, and festivals worldwide.

Josh co founded *Lean_In*, a nomadic movement series that has grown into the annual retreat *Lean_In_Nature*, inviting people into co-creative, embodied research. He has taught at CI hubs and circus events across Europe. His work invites participants into a dance of authenticity, where movement becomes a meeting place for truth and transformation.

INCLUSIVE AND SAFE SPACE

We are committed to creating an inclusive and safe space for all participants. This workshop is designed to be accessible to all and participants are welcome to let us know in advance about specific access needs.

Who’s the workshop for

Open to all levels. Whether you’re a seasoned pro or you've never done the practice before there is something for everyone. No previous dance experience required just a willingness to explore & create.

Where

Location will be given upon booking.

We will be dancing in the heart of Camberwell, the space has a kitchen available for use by participants, toilets and showers. Access to the hall is via a flight of stairs.

If you would like to attend but have financial concerns / are unable to purchase a ticket due to financial reasons please reach out - we will find the way with you.

This event is 18+

If you have any queries / questions / thoughts or just want to say hi please feel free to get in touch - leaninmovement123@gmail.com

In the afternoon sessions we will expand these explorations into the practice of Contact Improvisation to enhance our ability to interact and communicate expressively and playfully with ease and clarity. Drawing on our felt sense and somatic attunement through touch and gravity, we will revisit and refine Contact Improvisation skills and creative vocabularies, such as weight exchange, balance, support and lifts with a partner and in small ensemble situations. Each day we will take time to discuss or write reflectively about our personal and somatic discoveries. The Feldenkrais Method®, developed by Dr. Moshe Feldenkrais (1904-1984) is a gentle, embodied process focused on self-discovery, embodied thinking, creative wellbeing, and functional improvement. It invites participants to slow down, listen to internal sensations, and create new neural pathways that support creative choice making in action. This workshop is open to anyone interested in deepening their dance or movement practice. Thomas and Simonetta have been teaching Feldenkrais-informed dance classes around the globe for over 20 years and are world-leading researchers and artists in the field. Dr.Thomas Kampe (PhD) (he/him) has worked as a performer, artist, researcher and somatic educator across the globe for 40 years and was ‘Professor of Somatic Performance and Education’ at Bath Spa University (UK) between 2012 and 2022. Thomas initially trained in visual art and dance and is a teacher of the Feldenkrais Method ® which forms a rich foundation for his teaching, arts practice and research. He is interested in critical somatic arts legacies and his writings and performance works have been published internationally. He was editor of the Feldenkrais Research Journal Vol. 6 ‘Practices of Freedom: The Feldenkrais Method & Creativity’ in 2019, and recently co-edited JDSP Vol. 13.1 & 2 (2022): ‘Embodying Eco-Consciousness: Somatics, Aesthetic Practice and Social Action’. Simonetta Alessandri is an Italian dance artist & somatic educator based in London. She applies the Feldenkrais Method in dance & movement training and in performance making. She teaches at Trinity Laban, Goldsmiths University and London Contemporary Dance School. Her work is informed by more than 30 years of dancing, teaching and choreographing. Her choreography has been for dance companies, student pieces, large scale opera, improvised performance, site specific and movement direction for theatre. She was one of the few dance practitioners in Italy who began working with CI in the 90’s. She has been a guest teacher in Germany, Colombia, UK, Norway, Israel, France, Switzerland, Italy, Poland, Spain and Taiwan. She obtained the Post Graduate Diploma at London Contemporary Dance School; she is a qualified teacher of the Feldenkrais Method and she holds the Teacher Certificate of the Royal Academy of Dance. She is a founder member of CI@Goldsmiths London. https://bookwhen.com/cigoldsmiths/e/ev-swh5j-20260409100000

sessions.title: LONDON JAM
sessions.details:
https://www.eventbrite.com/e/london-jam-tickets-1990466643312?aff=oddtdtcreator&keep_tld=true

A CI jam to bring everyone together: London's CI teachers, organisers and you, the wider community for a time out to dance, lab and connect.


26th: Saturday 16:00 - 22:00

27th: Sunday 11:00-17:00


Our teaching and organising community is the foundation of London's CI community.
We want to celebrate being here together and meet you as a community, not just as individual practitioners.

Join us for one or two days of dancing, where you can fully let go—fall, fly, and be caught by the fabric of long-term, lush CI practices that our community holds. Experience CI as life integration where body meets mind and generates a collective field of care, curiosity and spirit.

We enter with as little agenda as possible, honouring the present moment that improvisation and jamming invite. Each day will be centred around spacious jams in the large Walworth Hall. Adjacent areas—the kitchen, living room, chill-out space and courtyard—give us room to chat, eat, rest, dream, and flow.

As our dancing and teaching community grows in size, practices, wisdom, and challenges, this event offers us a chance to jam our way into sensing who we are now and how we step into the future together.

Before and during the event, you are invited to share any questions you have about CI—technical, visionary, reflective, or concerning needs or serious concerns. We will dedicate 1.5 hours each day for teachers to explore these questions in small, spontaneous labs that you’re welcome to join on the spot.

And that’s really all there is to it!

This event is for people who consider CI an ongoing practice and who want to connect with the wider community through shared research and continuous exploration.

Please bring your own food. A microwave, cups, tea, and basic kitchen essentials are available to support your day.

sessions.title: Casa Tumbao: Classes, Social & Community
sessions.details: Casa Tumbao is a Cuban Salsa Community based in West London (W10 5XL). We host classes for all abilities, from first-timers to seasoned dancers, followed by a free social open to all, 9PM-11:30PM. We will teach you all the steps and the technicalities, but we are not a dance “school”, we are a Community. Our space is for trying something new, getting it wrong, experimenting, playing around, expressing yourself and connecting with yourself, others & the culture. Come for the dancefloor, come for the board games, come for the patties & drinks or come play around on our latin percussion instruments. There’s something for everyone as we curate this space to be our warm Neighbourhood Spot every Tuesday. Book your class via Luma (link in our instagram bio, or copy & paste the link below), send us a DM or pay £10 on the door. https://luma.com/user/casatumbao We also recognise that we are guests to Cuban culture. A culture that has so kindly welcomed us in. That’s why 10% of all our profits go to the AfroCuban Dance Festival’s Community Project, which supports the dancers, teachers and artists who keep this culture alive in Pogolotti, Havana. Tuesdays @ Casa Tumbao Running Order: 6:30-7:30 || 2 Classes Intro to Cuban Salsa Cuban Salsa Fundamentals 7:45-8:45 || 2 Classes Intermediate Class Advanced Class (5 Week Rotating Teacher Resiencies) 8:45-11:30 || Salsa Social (free & open to all) See you on the dancefloor!

sessions.title: Rueda Night
sessions.details: Come and join a fun and friendly worldwide community of Rueda de Casino dancers 🛞🕺💃🏻 Bournemouth has a dedicated Rueda de Casino night 🥳 To begin with there are 2 levels of classes: ** 7:30pm Rueda Flow 💨 ** For those of us obsessed with how far we can push the rueda game. This is a closed group for regular rueda de casino dancers, please message to express interest and to receive an invite. (Arrival from 7:15pm) ** 8:30pm Rueda FUNdamentals 🤩 ** This is suitable for ALL levels of rueda dancers to practise their skills (but you must dance salsa)! We will cover the core moves needed to join social ruedas, with a focus on fun, including calls not used in the Flow class. We will also introduce a partnerwork move each week to improve your social dancing repertoire! (Arrival from 8:15pm ** 9:15pm Salsa only social ** No partner or booking needed (but an invite is needed for the Flow group, and the timing of Flow can change when beginner’s courses are running). 💷 £8 for one class, £12 for both.

sessions.title: LA TIZA
sessions.details: La Tiza November is here! Step into a Cuban party like no other! Expect the best Cuban music, dance, live percussion and plenty of gozadera as we bring another night of Cuba to London. Whether you’ve never danced a step in your life or you’re already comfortable on the dancefloor, everyone is welcome. We are bringing you something new this month, a reparto class with Danny Garcia and the usual Salsa Freestyle with Yanet Fuentes. 🔥7.15pm – Reparto Class (Open Level): Learn the moves taking over Cuba right now, led by our guest teacher Danny Garcia, experience the energy behind one of the hottest sounds from the Island 💃🏻🕺🏽8.15 – Salsa Freestyle (Intermediate/Advanced Level): For those ready to challenge themselves, develop their technique and add even more sabor to their steps. Trained at the National School of Arts in Havana, Yanet brings a wealth of knowledge, technique, energy and authentic Cuban flavour to the dancefloor. Once classes are over, stay with us for a night of the very best Cuban salsa, timba and reparto with DJ GUI, expect live percussion, happy hour at the bar until 10pm, a dominoes table, we just need you to bring the vibes. 🇨🇺 Online Tickets Prices: 💃 Reparto Class with Danny Garcia + Party: £12 🔥 Intermediate/Advanced Salsa Class with Yanet Fuentes + Party: £12 🇨🇺 Both Classes + Party: £22 🎉 Party Only: £10

sessions.title: HFS Cuban Party w/ Cristian Mauricio & DJ Rich (Sat 14 November)
sessions.details: Hugs & Chaos w/ FRIENDS WKND is a concept bringing some of the international teachers who’ve had an impact on us to our local dancers in Redhill and the wider UK community. The aim is to expand the skills, knowledge and awareness of rueda and casino dancers and teachers in the UK, through amazing maestros who are approachable and who you can also enjoy social dancing with. The weekend is limited to 40 participants, to make sure everyone gets the most out of it. On this occasion, we’re bringing CRISTIAN MAURICIO, a dancer and teacher with deep knowledge and love for Cuban culture. Many know him as “El Rumbero de Chile”, but his talents are broad and definitely don’t stop there. Check below! From Santiago, Chile, now based in Barcelona 🇨🇱🇨🇺🇪🇸. He found Rueda de Casino at Club 440 in Santiago, and that one circle changed the entire course of his life. He went on to study at the Higher Institute of Art in Havana, danced as the Son dancer for the legendary Septeto Nacional de Ignacio Piñeiro, and became two-time World Rueda Champion with his group Tim Manana. The kind of CV that makes you forget he’s also just a genuinely lovely person to be around. This weekend he’s bringing his own method, Casino 5D, built from over 24 years of teaching and a lifetime of respect for where this dance actually comes from. Cristian teaches with patience, humour and a genuine love for passing this on — the kind of teacher you remember long after the weekend ends. Expect a Casino 5D bootcamp, Rueda (by him and us), Son and a weekend that’ll change how you hear the music, not just how you dance to it. 🔗Check him on: instagram.com/cristianmauriciovera Casino and Rueda de Casino Dancers from all over the UK and abroad will gather in Redhill for an amazing time dancing and celebrating together! If you are a high intermediate / advanced casino or rueda de casino dancer and you’d like to join, contact us soon to show interest! Places will sell out quickly! TIMES 🕛20:15 Doors opening 🕛20:30 Pre-Party Classes for beginners and 2 RUEDA classes by High Five Salsa 🕛21:30 Party with 100% Cuban music until 2am PARTY PRICES: 👉 EARLY BIRD by end of October: £10 party & class 👉 Tickets sold by 12 November: £10 party only / £12 party & class 👉 Tickets sold on the day/at the door: £15 📍Venue: Carrington School, Noke Drive (RH1 4AD). ASTRA BUILDING: https://youtube.com/shorts/Q6fShOP6P1E ❌Bar NOT available – BRING YOUR OWN DRINKS! 🚂The venue is only 5 min walk from the train and bus station. 🚗Plenty of car park spaces on the venue. Also possible to park on Noke Drive. Get your tickets now! Pictures and videos may be used during the event and used for promotion and/or on social media.
